content.thinking:
I'm sketching out a Genshin-style cel-shaded lava golem design, featuring dark basalt plates with glowing molten seams, gold filigree trim, and a flaming crystal core embedded in its chest.

Now I'm planning the golem's proportions and skeleton, aiming for roughly 3 meters tall with chunky oversized fists and shoulders against a small head, using a standard humanoid rig of hips, spine, neck, limbs, and extremities. I'm working out the rest pose coordinates—placing hips, spine joints, shoulders, and arm chains in 3D space to build an A-pose stance with arms angled outward and legs set apart.

Defining the spine bone chain...

Actually, I'll simplify by using absolute model-space coordinates everywhere with `at` and `dir`/`aim` rather than local bone rotations, avoiding roll confusion, and apply symmetry through loops. For the head, I'm picturing a boxy, chunky basalt helmet-like block.

I'm planning glowing yellow slit eyes using a textured plane, plus a separate jaw joint pivoting at the back-bottom of the head with glowing mouth and tusk-like basalt teeth inside. For arms, I'm setting shoulder joints symmetrically and building a shoulder-elbow-wrist chain per side, naming the joints so the wrist becomes the tip joint of each arm.

Hands get a full finger rig—four fingers plus a thumb, each with two joints, giving twenty finger joints across both hands. Tallying everything: spine, neck, head, and jaw joints, plus arms and fingers, plus a four-joint leg chain (hip, knee, ankle, toe) per leg, and I'm also considering decorative floating basalt shards near the shoulders as Genshin-style elemental motifs, along with hanging tassels and gold ornaments for flair. I'm now sketching out the cel-shaded material palette, starting with a dark basalt purple base color.

For the rock material I'm mottling the basalt tone for stone variation and considering a scales pattern with dark inked edges to give the plates a cracked, cellular look, all wrapped in the cel shading function so shadows derive automatically. For the lava, I'm keeping emissive parts as flat glowing colors rather than paint—layering orange sweep shapes with thinner yellow-core sweeps on top for hot seams, each wrapped in a glow effect, and now I'm mapping out where these molten crack lines run across the torso and limbs.

Now I'm planning to drape these crack sweeps directly onto the body surfaces using zigzag point paths, building a helper that creates each crack as a layered orange-and-yellow sweep lifted slightly off the surface. I'm also working out the overall structure: an inner glowing lava body (flat orange-to-bright gradient tones) with angular basalt plates sitting on top like armor, leaving visible glowing seams in the gaps between plates for that molten-core-with-cracked-shell effect, varying the seam colors from deep red-orange to brighter tones for visual interest.

Writing the plate placement logic...

Now I'm thinking about gold filigree trim: cuffs, arm rings, crown ornaments, and a chest brace to give that Genshin-style ornament-and-glow aesthetic. I want glowing rune decals as textured planes on the chest plates, plus a faceted icosahedron core crystal caged in gold rings as the elemental core centerpiece, surrounded by floating glowing shard motifs.

I'm also planning flame wisp effects from the shoulders and back using card textures with cel-shaded multi-tone flame svgs (red, orange, yellow), plus small floating ember spheres, and sketching out the body breakdown: chunky toed feet, pillar-like thighs and shins with molten gaps and gold anklets, and a gold tasseled belt over hanging stone loincloth slabs.

I'm continuing the structural plan — v-shaped barrel torso with a glowing molten abdomen and gold-caged core orb, massive basalt pauldrons with obsidian horn spikes, thick molten-jointed arms ending in knuckle-plated fists, a blocky horned helm with glowing eyes and mouth plus flame-hair cards, and a spiked basalt spine ridge with glowing seams running down the back. Given the ~1000 part budget, I'm thinking I'll need to use merged geometry for repeated small elements and aim to keep the total around 500 parts.

Now I'm working out the skeleton rig: hip root, a three-segment spine chain curving slightly forward as it rises, then a short neck chain terminating in a tip joint for the head, oriented along the tangent direction so it naturally points up and forward.

To simplify, I'll just give each part its own `at` and `dir` in model space. Checking the head's dimensions, I'm sizing it roughly 0.5 wide, 0.4 tall, 0.45 deep centered around [0,2.78,0.2], with horns extending up to about 3.2 total height.

Now I'm blocking out the torso with loft stations at the pelvis, waist, chest, and shoulders, defining width and depth at each level and attaching them to a spine/hip bone chain for the loft operation.

For the surface itself, this inner molten body glows orange and gets mostly covered by armor plates, leaving only gaps to show the glow. I'm weighing whether to keep it a flat emissive color like "#ff5a14" with yellow crack seams drawn on top for a Genshin-style cel look, versus a darker cel-shaded rock tone like "#7a2a1c", making sure plates cover enough area so the flat color doesn't read as too plain.

I'm leaning toward basalt plates with glowing molten seams visible at joints and gaps, and realizing I can fake the crack-glow effect without true emissive by coloring cell edges orange within the plate's color scale, which should read as molten seams between basalt segments under cel shading.

The Voronoi-style cracks actually look like nice cracked lava rock, so I'll apply this to the main limbs and torso as a cracked basalt skin with glowing seams throughout, then layer glowing 3D seams on top for the key structural lines and plates.

I'm working out seam widths and texel density — aiming for roughly 3cm seam lines, and checking that a 2048 paint resolution gives enough crispness for a ~40m² painted surface without blowing the atlas budget too much. Primary bodies get the crust material while plates get a separate mottled material with inked edges.

Now I'm defining the color palette: a purple-grey rock tone for the main plates, obsidian for horns and spikes, hot/orange/deep tones for glowing seams, gold tones for trim, and a warm glow color for crystal cores, plus a tooth tone.

Setting up imports...

Now working out leg skeleton details - hip joints positioned, ankle targets set, calculating limb lengths so the leg sits nearly straight with a slight knee bend forward.

Then I'm adding toe joints to the foot chain, considering whether to use a single toe joint or three separate ones for the front toes, leaving the role defaulted since it's not a critical hinge.

Now I'm thinking through the leg skinning, sweeping tapered geometry along the chain with decreasing radii from hip to ankle, and leaning toward a faceted low-sided ngon profile to get that chunky, angular basalt-golem look rather than smooth shading.

Hexagonal prisms feel right for basalt columns, so I'm using a six-sided ngon section for limbs with smooth skinning at the joints, then planning an armor helper that places plates around each limb tube by sampling positions along the path.

Writing plate geometry logic...

Since I'm passing plain computed vectors, the extrude won't know the nearest joint automatically, so I should pass the bone explicitly using `f.bone ?? undefined` to handle the Joint-or-null type properly.

Now I'm laying out the full model: defining side labels for left/right, then building the torso loft with a series of stations (position, width, height) running from hips up to chest, lofted with a catmull curve and bound to the hips/spine bones. I'm planning a crust-style paint with Voronoi seams and plated chest, but leaving the abdomen between pelvis and chest exposed with a strong glow.

I'm adding a molten belly band -- a glowing flat-orange sweep around the waist -- plus basalt crescent ribs, confirming that having it hidden under plates elsewhere is fine. Then I'm placing chest plates: pec slabs facing forward-outward, stacked ab plates below the sternum with gaps revealing the glow underneath, plus scapular, spine, and lat plates on the back and sides. I'm working out how to position these plates precisely by raycasting onto the torso's actual surface, writing a helper that fires a ray from far away toward the body to find the correct placement point.

Now I'm designing the gem-core orb mounted on the sternum hit point with a gold cage, then moving to shoulder pauldrons -- layered hexagonal domed caps built from a lathed profile, tilted outward, topped with gold rings and obsidian spikes, with a smaller second dome stacked below for a layered look, mounted at the shoulder joint. I'm also starting to lay out the arm geometry -- shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions -- working toward long golem arms with a hanging fist at the end.

Now I'm refining the arm pose into a slight A-pose with arms angled about 25-30° out from vertical, adjusting shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions so the big fists hang around waist height without touching the floor, and checking the overall horizontal span stays reasonable. I'm also sketching out a radius taper for the arm -- thinner upper arm narrowing at the elbow, then flaring into a bulky gauntlet-plated forearm toward the wrist.

For the hands, I'm planning an open, gorilla-like pose with a palm block oriented along the forearm direction and four curled fingers extending down-forward, built as two-joint chains with glowing molten fingertip cones, plus a thumb jutting out front, computing palm placement as an offset from the wrist along the arm's direction vector.

Still defining finger segments...

Now I'm tallying up total joint count: fingers alone give 30, plus spine, neck, head, jaw, legs with toes, and arms bring the estimate to around 70 joints, comfortably under the 160 limit.

I'm restructuring each finger to 2 joints instead of 3 for simplicity, bringing each hand to 10 joints and 20 total, with a wrist joint parenting the finger chains and a small glowing cone added at each fingertip for a molten-tip effect.

Now I'm adding knuckle plates and a gold cuff at the wrist using a lathe-revolved ring outline around the forearm's axis, planning a reusable collar function that takes position, direction, inner/outer radius, height, color, and bone to generate these bracer rings.

For the leg, I'm planning hex-column segments with gold glow-seam rings at the ankles and knees, then working out the vertical proportions: hip at y1.3, foot sole at y0, ankle around y0.25, with thigh width and leg spacing set relative to the hip radius.

I'm sizing the pelvis to span roughly 0.8 wide with hips at x±0.3, then blocking out the feet as tapered boxes with heel and toe sections positioned forward of the ankle joint.

For toes, I'm adding three hexagonal prism shapes spaced across the front of each foot, rigging them as child bones off the ankle so they can articulate, and capping the tips with small cone-shaped claws. I'm also making sure the feet sit flush with the ground plane by checking that the lowest points of each foot mesh land exactly at y=0.

Now I'm moving to the dorsal spikes along the spine—raycasting from behind the torso to find surface hit points, then attaching cone shapes at those positions with sizes increasing toward the top, plus small glowing base caps and flame-card plumes along the back. I'm writing an SVG flame texture with layered red, orange, and yellow cel-shaded sections for the fire effect.

Writing SVG code...

Then I need to apply a glow effect to the card meshes, and sketch out horn placement curving backward from the skull sides, obsidian with a gold tip ring.

Now I'm sketching the head structure: defining the skull core position sitting on the neck, with the torso top as the attachment point.

I'm shaping the cranium with brow ridge and cheek plates, then positioning glowing eye slits using a decal texture for an anime-style glow effect on the front of the head.

Adding a brow slab and front face mask plate, mimicking the obsidian masklike faces seen on Genshin golems with glowing eye slits set into the plate.

Now I'm planning the gold-trimmed chamfered mask outline, the glowing eye decals, and a gold fillet brow band, then moving to the jaw geometry hinged below the skull mass.

For the mouth, I'm adding upward lower tusks and downward upper teeth as cones, with a glowing orange slab between the jaws for the mouth interior, and sizing the head small relative to the 1.3-wide shoulders for a proportioned silhouette.

Going slightly stylized with a bigger head (0.6w x 0.5h), I'm positioning the cranium frustum between y 2.55-2.98 with the head centered around [0, 2.76, 0.2]. Now I'm planning floating obsidian shards orbiting near the shoulders—octahedrons scaled taller with glowing seams, three per side, possibly with a small inner glow spike or gold ring accent.

I'm adding glowing ember particles as merged tiny glow spheres attached to the spine bone, grouped by color for efficiency. For the molten crack seams, I'm designing a helper that drapes a zigzag polyline onto the body surface and sweeps a thin glowing tube along it, so I can scatter cracked orange seams across the waist, chest, and thighs using a reusable crack-drawing function.

Writing crack generator code...

For the gold filigree, I'm planning a lathe-round medallion for the belt buckle with a glowing center, plus draped gold chains or tassels across the chest using catenary sweeps with small beads.

I'm also designing ornate gold rims for the pauldrons, a crowned diadem spike on the head, gold horn tips and arm bands with glowing gems, plus gold belt plates with hanging tassels. For the chest and back I want a generic sunburst rune motif -- a concentric ring with radial ticks and a flame-ish diamond shape, careful to keep it original and avoid any game logos. My texture list is shaping up as flame, eye, rune, and tassel elements, with the first three glowing and the tassel staying matte gold and red.

Now I'm thinking about adding ember sparks and a gold filigree scroll decal for the plate surfaces -- thin scrolled gold lines on a transparent background applied to the chest and thigh plates as a flat decal facing outward along the plate's surface normal. Writing SVG code...

Then I'm starting to rough out the part counts, beginning with the torso loft and its roughly thirty plates.

Writing helper functions...

I'm verifying the cross-product identity confirms the thickness axis aligns correctly with the normal, and checking that the x/y parameters accept either array or Vector3 types.

Now I need to find where the `Joint` type is defined and exported, so I'll grep for its export along with the extrude options.
